title: Initial Access via MSKSSRV Kernel Driver Exploitation (CVE-2024-35250)
id: 1a8d7f9e-6c4b-4a3d-b8e2-a1b2c3d4e5f6
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2024-35250 where a local attacker sends crafted IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY request with KSPROPERTY_TYPE_UNSERIALIZESET flag to MSKSSRV kernel driver, indicating potential privilege escalation attempt.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2024/12/cisa-and-fbi-raise-alerts-on-exploited.html
    - https://devco.re/blog/2024/08/23/streaming-vulnerabilities-from-windows-kernel-proxying-to-kernel-part1-en/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-03
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.t1068
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith: '\mskssrv.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY'
            - 'KSPROPERTY_TYPE_UNSERIALIZESET'
            - 'Type3InputBuffer'
            - 'KsSynchronousIoControlDevice'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate system administration tools using kernel streaming APIs
    - Debugging or testing utilities interacting with kernel drivers
level: high

indicators.context: The name appears unencrypted in some of the malicious samples – it is the name of one of the threat actor’s components, so we decided to extend it to the APT as a whole.

One of them – ipv4.dll – has been placed by the APT with what is, in fact, a downloader for other malicious components.

When the target user runs Winbox Loader software (a utility used for Mikrotik router configuration), this connects to the router and downloads some DLLs (dynamic link libraries) from the router’s file system.
Following infection, Slingshot would load a number of modules onto the victim device, including two huge and powerful ones: Cahnadr, the kernel mode module, and GollumApp, a user mode module.
Canhadr, also known as NDriver, contains low-level routines for network, IO operations and so on.

During our research we also found a component called KPWS that turned out to be another downloader for Slingshot components.

status: experimental
description: Detects credential access attempts by DevilsTongue malware using Windows API calls to dump LSASS memory for credential theft.
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2021/07/15/protecting-customers-from-a-private-sector-offensive-actor-using-0-day-exploits-and-devilstongue-malware/
    - https://citizenlab.ca/2021/07/hooking-candiru-another-mercenary-spyware-vendor-comes-into-focus/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-03
tags:
    - attack.credential-access
    - attack.t1003.001
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\explorer.exe'
        GrantedAccess|contains:
            - '0x1010'
            - '0x1410'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate security tools accessing LSASS
level: high

pipeline.attack_summary: Attackers distribute Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS) via 'cracked' apps or by tricking users into copying and pasting malicious commands into the macOS Terminal. The initial access vector relies on social engineering to get users to execute terminal commands that download and run malware, bypassing Gatekeeper protections. AMOS uses persistence mechanisms like LaunchDaemons, collects sensitive data including browser credentials, crypto wallets, and system files, then exfiltrates this data via HTTP/HTTPS.

pipeline.attack_summary: Raspberry Robin is a worm that initially spreads through infected USB drives containing LNK files disguised as folders. It is part of a larger cybercriminal ecosystem where it serves as an infection vector for follow-on ransomware activities.

    - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-26084
    - https://confluence.atlassian.com/doc/confluence-security-advisory-2021-08-25-1077906215.html
    - https://github.com/h3v0x/CVE-2021-26084_Confluence
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-03
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1190
    - cve.2021-26084
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection_uri:
        cs-uri-stem|contains:
            - '/pages/createpage-entervariables.action'
    selection_query:
        cs-uri-query|contains:
            - 'queryString='
            - '${'
            - '[['
    condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative tools or scripts that use similar query parameters in non-malicious contexts
level: high

references:

    - https://confluence.atlassian.com/doc/confluence-security-advisory-2021-08-25-1077906215.html

tags:

        cs-uri-query|contains:
            - '${'
            - '[['
    condition: selection_ognl

level: high

pipeline.attack_summary: An unauthenticated attacker exploits CVE-2021-26084, a critical OGNL injection vulnerability in Atlassian Confluence Server and Data Center, to execute arbitrary code on affected systems. The attack leverages vulnerable endpoints like '/pages/createpage-entervariables.action' with attacker-controlled 'queryString' parameters, enabling remote code execution without authentication.

validation_issues.message: The 'cs-uri-stem' field is used for URI path matching, but the rule uses a hardcoded endpoint '/pages/createpage-entervariables.action'. While this is a known vulnerable endpoint, it may lead to over-specificity if attackers use alternative endpoints or variations. Consider broadening the match using |startswith or |contains with a more general pattern.

The rule includes 'queryString=' in the detection, which is specific to one PoC example. This may not cover all exploitation patterns; however, it's acceptable as part of a broader detection strategy.
